description: Comparative test across 10 mammals: is the 44-codon alternative (+2) frame ORF in the TMEM106A acceptor exon a selected feature or a byproduct of the native coding sequence?
code:
import requests, time, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from collections import Counter
S=requests.Session(); S.headers.update({"User-Agent":"gsdmd-cons"})
ENS="https://rest.ensembl.org"
def eseq(eid,typ="genomic"):
    for i in range(3):
        try:
            r=S.get(f"{ENS}/sequence/id/{eid}?type={typ}",timeout=20,
                    headers={"Content-Type":"application/json"})
            if r.status_code==200: return r.json()["seq"]
        except Exception: pass
        time.sleep(1)
    return None

EXON={"human":"ENSE00001627792","chimp":"ENSPTRE00000092176","macaque":"ENSMMUE00000101221",
      "mouse":"ENSMUSE00001226766","rat":"ENSRNOE00000265799","rabbit":"ENSOCUE00000229960",
      "dog":"ENSCAFE00845047846","cow":"ENSBTAE00000072552","pig":"ENSSSCE00000202365",
      "opossum":"ENSMODE00000157588"}

bases="TCAG"; aas="FFLLSSSSYY**CC*WLLLLPPPPHHQQRRRRIIIMTTTTNNKKSSRRVVVVAAAADDEEGGGG"
CODON={a+b+c:aas[i] for i,(a,b,c) in enumerate([(x,y,z) for x in bases for y in bases for z in bases])}
def tr_(s): return "".join(CODON.get(s[i:i+3].upper(),"X") for i in range(0,len(s)-2,3))
SYN={}
for c,a in CODON.items(): SYN.setdefault(a,[]).append(c)
def orf(s):           # ORF length in the +2 (chimeric) frame, codons until first stop
    a=tr_(s[2:]); l=a.find("*"); return len(a) if l<0 else l

seqs={}
for sp,eid in EXON.items():
    s=eseq(eid)
    if s is None or len(s)!=141: print(f"{sp}: fetch problem (len {None if s is None else len(s)})"); continue
    seqs[sp]=s.upper()

print("validation: native phase-0 frame of the 141-nt exon must give 47 clean codons\n")
hdr=f"{'species':9s} {'native 47aa peptide':49s} stops  alt(+2) ORF"
print(hdr); print("-"*len(hdr))
nat={}
for sp,s in seqs.items():
    p=tr_(s); nat[sp]=p
    print(f"{sp:9s} {p:49s} {p.count('*'):5d}  {orf(s):6d}")

# per-species codon-usage-weighted synonymous shuffle of the SAME exon
rng=np.random.default_rng(7); N=5000
rows=[]
for sp,s in seqs.items():
    codons=[s[i:i+3] for i in range(0,141,3)]
    cnt=Counter(codons)
    W={}
    for aa,cods in SYN.items():
        a=np.array([cnt.get(x,0)+1 for x in cods],dtype=float); W[aa]=a/a.sum()
    cols=[]
    for c in codons:
        aa=CODON[c]; cods=np.array(SYN[aa]); cols.append(cods[rng.choice(len(cods),size=N,p=W[aa])])
    mat=np.array(cols)
    null=np.array([orf("".join(mat[:,j])) for j in range(N)])
    real=orf(s); pv=(np.sum(null>=real)+1)/(N+1)
    rows.append((sp,real,float(np.median(null)),float(np.percentile(null,95)),pv))

print("\nspecies    observed  null_median  null_p95   p")
for sp,real,med,p95,pv in rows:
    print(f"{sp:9s} {real:8d} {med:12.0f} {p95:9.0f}  {pv:.3f}")
nsig=sum(1 for r in rows if r[4]<0.05)
print(f"\nspecies with p < 0.05: {nsig}/{len(rows)}  (no multiple-testing correction applied)")

# identity of the native vs alternative frame peptide, human as reference
ref="human"
def ident(a,b): return 100*sum(x==y for x,y in zip(a,b))/min(len(a),len(b))
print("\nper-species identity to human, native frame vs chimeric (+2) frame:")
for sp in seqs:
    if sp==ref: continue
    altH=tr_(seqs[ref][2:]); altS=tr_(seqs[sp][2:])
    print(f"  {sp:9s} native {ident(nat[ref],nat[sp]):5.1f}%   alt(+2) {ident(altH,altS):5.1f}%")

fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(9,4.2))
sp_names=[r[0] for r in rows]; x=np.arange(len(rows))
ax.bar(x-0.2,[r[1] for r in rows],0.4,label="observed +2 frame ORF",color="#c0392b")
ax.bar(x+0.2,[r[2] for r in rows],0.4,label="null median",color="#6e8fb2")
ax.errorbar(x+0.2,[r[2] for r in rows],
            yerr=[np.zeros(len(rows)),[r[3]-r[2] for r in rows]],fmt="none",ecolor="#33475e",capsize=3)
for i,r in enumerate(rows): ax.text(i,max(r[1],r[3])+1.5,f"p={r[4]:.2f}",ha="center",fontsize=7)
ax.set_xticks(x); ax.set_xticklabels(sp_names,rotation=35,ha="right")
ax.set_ylabel("ORF length in the +2 frame, codons")
ax.set_title("TMEM106A acceptor exon: alternative-frame ORF against a codon-usage-weighted null\n"
             "(5,000 permutations per species; bar caps mark the null 95th percentile)",fontsize=10)
ax.legend(fontsize=8,frameon=False); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
